adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In a JS object literal those expressions evaluate immediately to a string (likely `"[object Object]"`), so both entries target the same literal property name and the latter overwrites the former. This does not create a pattern/index-signature; it creates (at most) a single optional key named `"[object Object]"`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, real token fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` will be dropped in sync mode, leaving essentially only `access_token` in `data`, matching the finding’s claim that expiry fields won’t be preserved when saving refreshed credentials.
